He played [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Notre Dame]]. ==Early development== Colson, the son of a former [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]] player who went into college coaching, played high school basketball in that state at [[St. Andrew's School (Rhode Island)|St. Andrew's School]] in [[Barrington, Rhode Island|Barrington]], as well as [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball with Boston Area Basketball Club. He developed as a pure post player, but was abnormally short for the position—during a basketball camp in summer 2013, he measured at {{convert|6|ft|4.5|in|m|abbr=on}} in shoes. Despite his physical stature, advanced statistics showed him to be unusually effective in the frontcourt; in July 2013, Colson had the top [[player efficiency rating]] (PER) among frontcourt players in [[Nike Inc.|Nike's]] Elite Youth Basketball League.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2016/11/30/notre-dame-fighting-irish-acc-bonzie-colson |title=Undersized and underrated, Bonzie Colson has become Notre Dame's star |first=Luke |last=Winn |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=November 30, 2016 |accessdate=March 30, 2017}} While Colson was largely ignored by major programs as a frontcourt prospect, [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] assistant [[Martin Ingelsby]], who went on to become head coach at [[Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens men's basketball|Delaware]], had a very different view, based on Colson's production in both high school and AAU play, as well as a disproportionate wingspan of {{convert|6|ft|11.5|in|m|abbr=on}}. When Colson visited Notre Dame in September 2013, the coaching staff made Nike's PER study a major part of its pitch, convincing him that the Fighting Irish program, devoted to offensive efficiency, would be the best fit for a player of his type. He would commit to Notre Dame that October. ==College career== In Colson's freshman season at Notre Dame, he came off the bench for 31 of his 32 appearances. He recorded a 17-point performance in a win over [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] in the semi-final game of the ACC Tournament. At the end of the season, he was named Notre Dame Newcomer of the Year. Colson appeared in 36 games in his sophomore season, starting in 24. He recorded the first 30-point game of his career on January 16, 2016, leading Notre Dame to its first victory over Duke at [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]]. In his junior season, Colson became Notre Dame's leading scorer (17.8 points per game; 9th in the ACC), led the ACC in rebounding (10.1 per game) and was eighth in blocks per game (1.4),{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21664213/bilas-index-volume-1-looks-best-68-teams-college-basketball |title=Bilas Index: A full look at the best 68 teams in college hoops |first=Jay |last=Bilas |authorlink=Jay Bilas |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=December 5, 2017 |accessdate=December 5, 2017}} and was named to the All-ACC first team.{{cite web|title=ACC ANNOUNCES ALL-CONFERENCE TEAM, POSTSEASON AWARDS|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/acc-announces-all-conference-team-postseason-awards-03-05-2017|website=theacc.com|accessdate=12 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170306210527/http://www.theacc.com/news/acc-announces-all-conference-team-postseason-awards-03-05-2017|archive-date=2017-03-06|url-status=dead}} He was also the first player shorter than 6' 7" to lead the ACC in rebounding since 1958. Prior to the 2017–18 season, Colson was named the preseason ACC Player of the Year and a first-team preseason All-American by the [[Associated Press]].{{cite news|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2017-11-06/college-basketball-michigan-states-bridges-tops-ap-preseason |title=Michigan State's Bridges tops AP preseason All-America team |publisher=[[NCAA.com]] |date=November 6, 2017 |accessdate=November 9, 2017}} After missing 15 games during the regular season with a broken foot, Colson broke his left foot again in Notre Dame's NIT tournament game against [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]].{{cite web |last1=Axson |first1=Scooby |title=Notre Dame's Bonzie Colson injures foot again |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/21/notre-dame-bonzie-colson-foot-injury |website=SI.com |date=March 21, 2018 |accessdate=24 November 2018 |language=en}} In 2017–18, he averaged 19.7 points per game (3rd in the ACC), 10.1 rebounds (3rd), 1.7 steals (6th), and 2.2 blocks (5th).{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/conferences/Atlantic-Coast-Conference/1/stats/2018/Averages/All/All/Season/All/trb/desc/1/|title=Atlantic Coast Conference Stats - RealGM|website=basketball.realgm.com}} ==Professional career== ===Canton Charge (2018–2019)=== On September 18, 2018, Colson signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|title=Cavaliers' Bonzie Colson: Signs contract with Cavs|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/cavaliers-bonzie-colson-signs-contract-with-cavs/|website=NBA.com|accessdate=October 16, 2018|date=September 18, 2018}} On October 13, he was waived by the Cavaliers,{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Waive Bonzie Colson, Kobi Simmons and Emanuel Terry|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/waive-colson-simmons-terry-181013|website=NBA.com|accessdate=October 16, 2018|date=October 13, 2018}} but was added to the roster of the Cavs' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Canton Charge]].{{cite web|title=Canton Charge 2018-19 Training Camp Roster|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-2018-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2018|accessdate=October 21, 2018|archive-date=July 15, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200715165026/https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-2018-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} In his first G League game, a 101–89 loss to the [[Wisconsin Herd]], Colson led the team with 23 points and 15 rebounds, shooting 10-of-18 from the floor.{{cite news |title=Charge can't connect in season-opening loss at Wisconsin |url=https://www.cantonrep.com/sports/20181103/charge-cant-connect-in-season-opening-loss-at-wisconsin |accessdate=November 4, 2018 |work=[[Canton Repository]] |date=November 3, 2018}} For the G League team, in 23 games he averaged 15.5 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks per game.{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Bonzie-Colson-Jr/Summary/52345|title=Bonzie Colson, Jr. Player Profile, Milwaukee Bucks - RealGM|website=basketball.realgm.com}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2019)=== On January 15, 2019, Colson was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. Under the terms of the deal, he split time with the Bucks' G League affiliate, the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite web|title=Bucks Signed Bonzie Colson To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/bucks-signed-bonzie-colson-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 15, 2019|accessdate=January 15, 2019}} For the G League team, in 23 games he averaged 14.3 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 0.8 blocks per game. Colson made his NBA debut on February 25, 2019, against the [[Chicago Bulls]], playing three minutes in the Bucks 117–106 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.brewhoop.com/2019/2/25/18240662/rapid-recap-bucks-rock-fiserv-forum-south-win-117-106|title=Rapid Recap: Bucks Rock Fiserv Forum South, Win 117-106|first=Riley|last=Feldmann|website=BrewHoop.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=February 25, 2019|access-date=February 27, 2019}} On March 31, Colson started his first NBA game against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] and in that game, he managed to score 15 points and grabbed 16 rebounds in 41 minutes of playing time.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bucks-bonzie-colson-huge-double-double-out-of-nowhere/|title=Bucks' Bonzie Colson: Huge double-double out of nowhere|website=cbssports.com|date=March 31, 2019|accessdate=April 1, 2019}} On July 21, 2019, Colson was waived by the Bucks.{{cite web|title=Bonzie Colson: Waived by Milwaukee|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bonzie-colson-waived-by-milwaukee/|website=CBS Sports|accessdate=July 29, 2019|date=July 21, 2019}} ===Darüşşafaka (2019–2020)=== On July 30, 2019, Colson signed with [[Darüşşafaka Basketbol|Darüşşafaka]].{{cite web|title=Darussafaka inks forward Colson|url=https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/9u59ak7c9sk5kiy3/darussafaka-inks-forward-colson|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190730100610/https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/9u59ak7c9sk5kiy3/darussafaka-inks-forward-colson|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 30, 2019|date=July 30, 2019|website=eurocupbasketball.com|accessdate=July 30, 2019}} Colson and the team mutually parted ways on April 24, 2020. Colson averaged 12.2 points and 5.1 rebounds per game in the Turkish League and 10.8 points and 5.0 rebounds in [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] play.{{cite web|title= Darussafaka part ways with Bonzie Colson|url= https://www.aa.com.tr/en/sports/basketball-darussafaka-part-ways-with-bonzie-colson/1817523|date=April 24, 2020|website=aa.com.tr|accessdate=June 26, 2020}} ===SIG Strasbourg (2020–2021)=== On August 31, 2020, Colson signed with [[SIG Strasbourg]].{{cite web|title=Bonzie Colson Joins SIG Strasbourg|url=https://www.ballersabroad.com/news/bonzie-colson-joins-sig-strasbourg|date=August 31, 2020|website=ballersabroad.com|accessdate=August 31, 2020}}{{Dead link|date=October 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}{{cite web|title=Strasbourg Signs Bonzie Colson Jr., ex Darussafaka|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/news/642954/Strasbourg-signs-Bonzie-Colson-Jr.,-ex-Darussafaka|date=August 31, 2020|website=eurobasket.com|accessdate=August 31, 2020}} He was named player of the week on October 14, after posting 24 points, nine rebounds and two assists in a win against [[Orléans Loiret Basket]].{{cite web |title=Bonzie Colson Jr. claims French Jeep ELITE ProA weekly honour |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/news/648512/Bonzie-Colson-Jr.-claims-French-Jeep-ELITE-ProA-weekly-honour |website=Eurobasket |accessdate=October 14, 2020 |date=October 14, 2020}} In 49 games he averaged 18.1 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 0.6 blocks per game. In games in the Jeep Elite he was 2nd in the league with 18.4 points per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/turkey-super-league/2022.html|title=Türkiye Sigorta Basketbol Süper Ligi - 2021-22 Standings and Stats|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} He was selected [[Basketball Champions League MVP|Most Valuable Player]] for the regular season of [[2020–21 Basketball Champions League]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.championsleague.basketball/en/20-21/news/colson-named-mvp-of-the-season|title=Colson named MVP of the Season|date=7 May 2021|access-date=7 May 2021|work=[[Basketball Champions League]]}} ===Pınar Karşıyaka (2021–2022)=== On July 10, 2021, Colson signed with [[Karşıyaka Basket|Pınar Karşıyaka]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]]{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/pinar-karsiyaka-lands-bonzie-colson/|title=Pinar Karsiyaka lands Bonzie Colson|last=|first=|date=July 10, 2021|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 10, 2021|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} In 42 games he averaged 15.9 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 0.8 blocks per game. In games in the Turkish Super League he was 7th in the league with 16.9 points per game, 7th with 7.0 rebounds per game, 7th with 1.6 steals per game, and 9th with 0.8 blocks per game. ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2022–2024)=== [[File:2022-12-22 ALBA Berlin gegen Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C. (EuroLeague 2022-23) by Sandro Halank–011.jpg|thumb|200px|Colson in 2022]] On June 22, 2022, he signed with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/maccabi-tel-aviv-signs-bonzie-colson/|title=Maccabi Tel Aviv signs Bonzie Colson|last=|first=|date=June 22, 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=June 22, 2022|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }} ===Fenerbahçe (2024–2026)=== [[File:Bonzie Colson 50 Fenerbahçe Basketbol TBSL 20241006 (3).jpg|thumb|right|Colson with [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]] in 2024]] On June 28th, 2024, Colson signed a three-year deal with Turkish powerhouse [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe Beko]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2024/6/bonzie-colson-fenerbahce-beko-da|title=Bonzie Colson Fenerbahçe Beko’da|last=|first=|date=June 28, 2024|website=|publisher=[[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]]|language=tr|access-date=June 28, 2024}} On May 25, 2025, he helped Fenerbahçe to their second EuroLeague championship in [[Abu Dhabi]].{{Cite web |date=2025-05-25 |title=Fenerbahce crowned 2025 champion with 70-81 win over Monaco |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/fenerbahce-crowned-2025-champion-with-70-81-win-over-monaco/ |access-date=2025-05-25 |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}} ===Return to Maccabi Tel Aviv (2026–present)=== On June 28, 2026, Colson signed a 2-year deal with his former club, Israeli powerhouse [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/bonzie-colson-returns-for-second-stint-with-maccabi/|title=Bonzie Colson returns for second stint with Maccabi|date=June 28, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=June 28, 2026}} The Israeli club paid the buyout clause of 200k dollars, and will pay Colson a salary of 1.5 million dollars a year. ==Playing style== In a 2016 story, ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' writer Luke Winn called Colson "one of college basketball's greatest anomalies." While Colson was not much larger than in high school—by then, he claimed to be {{convert|6|ft|5|in|m|abbr=on}} tall with a {{convert|7|ft|m|abbr=on}} wingspan—Notre Dame was frequently playing him as a [[Center (basketball)|center]] alongside four guards, three of them taller than Colson. As early as his high school and AAU days, according to Winn, "he knew how to work angles to get off all kinds of funky shots" and "played with a chip on his shoulder due to being ignored by many big-time schools". In his final two seasons at Notre Dame, Colson began to include [[Three-point field goal|three-pointers]] in his skill set, enabling him to also play as a [[stretch four]] in some Notre Dame lineups.
